Subject: Chain-of-custody process for 3P claim evidence — MSA indemnity ask

Hi Elizabeth,

Thanks again for the call this morning. To move the indemnity discussion forward on our side, legal asked for a short, auditable chain-of-custody workflow for any evidence Acme might provide if a third-party IP claim arises.

Two asks from our procurement/legal team:

1) Can Acme confirm the types of evidence you would reasonably provide (logs, model prompts, ingestion manifests, human reviewer notes)?
2) Can you share a preferred file-handoff protocol and retention period (SFTP, secure Drive share, signed manifest with timestamps)?

I attached a very small evidence manifest template and a sample chain-of-custody pdf that our ops/legal teams prefer. If you can populate the manifest for a hypothetical claim (or send your template), we can reconcile it against the MSA redlines Kimberly circulated.

Next step: if possible please reply by end of week with either your template or a short bulleted protocol. If not, can we schedule a 30-min sync next Tues? Ben will join to capture the operational steps.

Thanks,

Marcus
VP, Legal & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- Acme_evidence_manifest_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
- chain_of_custody_template.pdf (PDF)
From: Legal Ops <legalops@acmecorp.com>

Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Chain-of-custody process for 3P claim evidence — MSA indemnity ask

Marcus,

Thanks for the template — useful. High level response now, formal template attached by tomorrow:

- Evidence types: we can provide ingestion manifests, server-side logs (timestamps + request IDs), a redacted prompt bundle, and reviewer notes where available. We cannot provide raw customer content without a lawful basis; that will be redacted.
- File-handoff: we prefer an SFTP drop with an accompanying signed manifest. For urgent claims, we can provide a secure ShareLink (read-only) and a notarized manifest within 48 hours.
- Retention: standard 12 months on secured storage, 30 days for expedited claim artifacts; subject to legal hold.

We'll attach Acme_Evidence_Protocol_v1.docx tomorrow. If Kimberly or Ben want to flag anything that would block us from accepting the MSA redline (e.g., overbroad evidence requests), call that out and we'll propose alternatives.

—Legal Ops (on behalf of Elizabeth)

Subject: Re: Chain-of-custody process for 3P claim evidence — MSA indemnity ask

Elizabeth / Legal Ops,

Appreciate the quick thumbs-up. A couple of clarifying points from our side (Kimberly asked me to surface these before we accept any final wording):

- Scope: Redwood cannot be required to preserve raw customer content that would expose third parties; acceptable scope should be metadata + redacted artifacts unless a court order requires otherwise.
- Timing & SLA: for a defended claim we ask for a 72-hour initial evidence handoff window (manifest + secure link) and a defined escalation path for additional data. If Acme needs more time, we can document a specific exception in the order form.
- Cost allocation: if evidence preservation requires non-trivial engineering work (for custom log exports), we need to have a mechanism to bill or agree to a cap. Our procurement prefers an hourly estimate + not-to-exceed cap rather than an open-ended obligation.

Ben, can you draft simple language for the order form that: (a) limits discoverable artifacts to metadata + redacted content unless compelled; (b) requires a signed manifest with timestamps; (c) creates a per-incident engineering cap? I attached a one-page redline excerpt of the MSA for reference.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Marcus

Subject: Re: Chain-of-custody process for 3P claim evidence — MSA indemnity ask

Thanks Marcus — drafted language below and attached as a short order form clause. Elizabeth/Legal Ops: please review and tell us if this is implementable from Acme's side.

Proposed clause (Order Form — Evidence Preservation):

"In the event of a third-party claim alleging IP infringement, Customer shall provide Redwood with a signed evidence manifest describing the types of materials being supplied (e.g., ingestion manifests, server logs, redacted prompt bundles, reviewer notes). Redwood's obligations are limited to receiving and preserving metadata and redacted artifacts unless Redwood is served with a lawful compulsion (court order, subpoena) requiring production of raw customer content. Customer will deliver the initial manifest and secure transfer link within seventy-two (72) hours of notice of the claim. If additional, bespoke data exports are requested that require engineering work, Customer agrees to reimburse Redwood at Redwood's then-current professional services rates up to a not-to-exceed amount of USD 8,000 per claim; Redwood will notify Customer before incurring engineering costs beyond that cap." 

If that matches Acme's operating model, we can fold into the order form and mark the MSA redline resolved. If Acme needs a different cap or SLA, let us know and we'll update.

Ben Carter
Senior Contracts Manager
Redwood Inference
